title: Electricity-grid chain

chokepoint.physics: Transformer cores need grain-oriented silicon steel, a patented, capital-heavy mill process. The equipment stage downstream is genuinely diffuse (HHI 0.073, 182 exporters) and constrained by factory lead-time, not concentration - but the steel it is built from is the tightest node in the chain, and tightening

eyebrow: Product-chain pilot · the wires that carry it all
h1: The ore is fine — the transformer is the bottleneck
deck: Copper and aluminium are abundant and diversified, and the equipment queues are real: a large power transformer can take up to four years to procure, and the world must roughly double its grid by 2040. But one material inside that equipment is not diffuse at all. Grain-oriented electrical steel — the transformer core — is the most concentrated node we measure in this chain, more so than the transformers themselves.
byline: copper & aluminium (abundant) ≠ grain-oriented electrical steel (HHI 0.164, rising) ≠ transformers & cables (years-long queues) ≠ the network
correction: You cannot mine your way to a working grid — but nor is the material question closed. Copper and aluminium are not the binding constraint; large power transformers take up to four years to order and HVDC cables more than five, while ~1,500 GW of renewables sit in connection queues. The correction to our own earlier framing: the core steel is TIGHTER than the equipment it goes into. Grain-oriented electrical steel exports run at HHI 0.164 against 0.073 for transformers, and the gap has been widening since 2019.

sections.h2: 1 · The chokepoint is the equipment — and the one steel inside it

panels.text: A large power transformer — the workhorse that steps voltage up and down across the grid — can now take up to four years to procure, with prices sharply higher. HVDC cables run even longer, more than five years. These lead times, not any raw material, are what actually delay connecting new generation and reinforcing the network.
panels.note: IEA, Building the Future Transmission Grid; US DOE.

panels.h3: Why: electrical steel and skilled winding
panels.text: Transformer cores need grain-oriented electrical steel, and building a transformer takes skilled winding and testing that cannot be rushed. We had asserted the steel was made by "a small number of mills" while the chain diagram filed it with copper and aluminium as abundant. Measured, it is neither abundant nor diffuse: HHI 0.164, China 28.8% and Japan 24.3% — 53% from two countries, 61% from three. The transformers built from it score 0.073, copper wire 0.066, high-voltage cable 0.060. The core input is more than twice as concentrated as the equipment.
panels.note: Computed from CEPII BACI HS17, codes 722511 + 722611, exporter value shares, 3-year mean 2022–2024 — grid-chain/out/goes.json.
panels.flag: the tightest node in the chain is a steel, not a metal

panels.text: GOES export concentration has risen every year but one since 2019: 0.111, 0.127, 0.122, 0.146, 0.167, 0.188 in 2024. China went from 27.3% of exports in 2022 to 31.7% in 2024; Russia, at 8%, is sanctions-exposed supply on top. A chain whose tightest node is getting tighter is a different planning problem from one with a stable bottleneck.
panels.note: Same series, annual. Trade is not capacity: export shares say who SELLS, not who can MAKE. A producer consuming its own output at home is understated — China notably — so 0.164 is a FLOOR on the real concentration, and the direction of that error is known.

sections.h2: 2 · The metals are abundant — the steel is the exception

panels.h3: Copper and aluminium are not the wall here
panels.text: Grids run on copper and aluminium, both diversified and recyclable. Aluminium even substitutes for copper in many overhead lines. Copper has its own longer-term tightness — a demand-versus-mine-timeline story told in the copper chain — but for building the grid this decade, neither metal is the binding constraint. This holds for the conductors and NOT for the core steel, which is the section above: grouping the three together was our error, and it survived because nobody had measured the third one.
panels.flag: see the copper chain for the metal's own clock

panels.h3: A grid that has to double

cards.d: The IEA estimates the world must add or refurbish ~80 million km of grid by 2040 — roughly the length of the entire existing network, built again.
Around 1,500 GW of renewable projects — many times a year's additions — sit in interconnection queues, waiting on grid capacity that isn't there.
Grids rarely make headlines, but they gate solar, wind, EV charging and data centres alike — the chokepoint downstream of every clean-energy chain.

trade_intro: BACI carries copper wire, aluminium conductor, transformers and switchgear, but a transformer's customs origin is its assembly plant, not the electrical-steel mill or the order backlog behind it. Read the shares below as equipment-trade positions; the binding constraint — manufacturing lead time — is not visible in trade data.
